summary:
NandaView shows historical climate analogs to compare three rice-based rotations in Guanacaste, Costa Rica, under identical past weather: rice followed by melon (the reference), cowpea, or forage sorghum. Using daily NASA POWER climate data (1981–2026) and NOAA's El Niño index (ONI), it finds seasons similar to a chosen scenario (strong El Niño, Neutral, La Niña or "Like 2026") and runs each rotation through them with the FAO-56 soil water balance.

For each rotation it reports crop water demand, water deficit and days of water stress as a range across similar years not a single guess and states what remains unverified. Since El Niño linked drought is a major risk for Guanacaste farmers and the wrong crop choice can waste a season, this lets growers and advisors see how each option behaved under comparable conditions before they plant.

The name honors Nandayure, a Guanacaste canton whose name comes from the language of the Chorotega, the region's indigenous people, and is often read as "stream" a reminder that water has always shaped life in this land, and that replaying how it behaved in past seasons can help today's growers farm with the memory of the land behind them.
details:
What it does and how it works

  • Matches past seasons to a chosen scenario with KNN on rainfall, ET₀, temperature, hot days and ONI.
  • Runs each rotation through a FAO-56 daily soil water balance (Penman-Monteith ET₀).
  • Reports p10/p50/p90 ranges (the low end, typical case and high end across the similar past seasons), calculated as differences against the rice → melon baseline for each year. These show variation between past years, not the probability of an outcome.
  • Includes a map of the 11 Guanacaste cantons, Sentinel-2 and OpenAerialMap imagery, and English/Spanish support.

Data sources

  • NASA POWER climate data: 16,754 days, with 42 complete years (1984–2025).
  • NOAA ONI for El Niño phases.
  • SoilGrids for soil water retention (estimated, not measured).
  • CHIRPS rainfall, used to compare against POWER.
  • Crop calendars from MAG, INTA, UCR and FAO studies.

Benefits and impact

  • Growers and advisors can compare water demand, deficit and stress days between rotations before planting, so they can avoid wasting a season on the wrong crop.
  • Results are honest ranges, with no claimed yield, profit or "winning" rotation.

Tools

  • Backend and science: Python, FastAPI, Pydantic, rio-tiler and pytest (96% coverage of the simulation code).
  • Frontend: React, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind, MapLibre, Recharts, Vitest and Playwright.
  • CI and deployment: GitHub Actions.
  • AI assistants: Codex, Cursor and Claude Code.

Creativity and factors considered

  • "Replaying the land's memory" instead of forecasting the weather.
  • POWER reports about half the rainfall of CHIRPS and IMN before 2005, and no correction is applied.
  • Small samples in strong El Niño scenarios (3 analogs instead of 5), so the ranges there rest on few seasons.
  • Backtest against the real 2015 and 2023 seasons.
  • No invented data in real runs (synthetic fixtures are labeled as mock), and 2026 is never used as one of the similar past years.
  • Rainfed rather than flooded rice, and estimated rather than measured soil.
  • This is a regional pilot, and crop parameters and farm-level use still need validation.
